items.why_relevant: Core rigid-body projection: lines 162-189. Builds 3×6 Jacobian matrix (identity for translational part, -skew-symmetric for rotational part), solves regularized normal equations g_reg = g + reg*I, applies projection via Jacobian. Uses mass-weighted least-squares fit to find best-fit translational velocity (v_com) and angular velocity (ω) for each water triplet.

OU noise sampling uses Cholesky on the error covariance G = J^T*diag(m)*J: samples z ~ N(0,I), solves L*ξ = √(kT)*z, projects back via J. This is CORRECT for the null space of J, but the magnitude of noise in each DOF may be wrong if J's rows have different magnitudes.

The Jacobian J structure for rigid-body projection: rows 1-3 are [I, 0], rows 4-6 are [0, -[r]_×]. The magnitude of ||J[i,:]||_2 differs by system-dependent factors (depends on r_i magnitude). items.excerpt: Optimal rotation via Horn's (1987) unit-quaternion method. We deliberately use the 4x4 eigenvalue formulation rather than SVD/Kabsch: TIP3P water is PLANAR, so the 3x3 cross-covariance is rank-deficient and the SVD's smallest singular vectors flip sign discontinuously between steps -> a discontinuous rotation matrix that injects spurious work and detonates energy conservation over a trajectory. Horn's largest-eigenvalue quaternion is well-separated and continuous through the planar case, and always yields a proper rotation.
items.why_relevant: Horn method was specifically chosen to avoid SVD sign-flip discontinuities. However, the quaternion eigenvalue computation (jnp.linalg.eigh, line 383) and rotation matrix assembly (lines 388-404) are FMA-sensitive.

findings.why_relevant: delta_o = pos_oxygen_c - pos_oxygen_new in settle_positions minimum-image correction. SETTLE geometry is sub-Ångström (per code comment line 158-159), so |delta_o| <= ~1 Å. For box >= 25 Å, delta_o/box in [-1/box, +1/box] ≈ [-0.04, 0.04]. Reachable range does NOT include tie-point region (0.5, 1) or (-1, -0.5). Verdict: COLD/UNREACHABLE. Confirmed per code documentation at lines 158-165.

dH = r_H_unc - r_O_unc in _r_step_conserve_angular_momentum, unwrapping H relative to O. Code docstring (line 737-741) explicitly states: 'shift_fn wraps atoms individually... water molecules near periodic boundary may have O at x≈0 and H at x≈L_box'. Physical scenario: true O at x=-0.04 wraps to L_box-0.04, true H at x=0.92 wraps to 0.92, giving dH = 0.92 - (L_box-0.04) = 1-L_box, so dH/box ≈ -1+1/L_box. Symmetric case: O at 0.04 wraps to 0.04, H at -0.92 wraps to L_box-0.92, giving dH/box ≈ 1-1/L_box. Combined range: dH/box in [-1+ε, 1-ε] where ε ≈ 1/L_box < 0.05. This range INCLUDES 0.5 and -0.5. Tie-point region (0.5,1) ∪ (-1,-0.5) IS REACHABLE. Verdict: REACHABLE.

dx = x_con - x_unc in settle_langevin R-step momentum correction (lines 1260-1262). Code comment (lines 1254-1259) states: 'shift_fn may wrap x_unc across periodic boundary while settle_positions reconstructs x_con in unwrapped frame of positions_old, so raw difference can jump by full box vector... spurious ~box-sized impulse that detonates integrator'. Physical mechanism: (1) x_unc wrapped to [0,L_box) by shift_fn, (2) x_con from settle_positions operating in frame of positions_old (previous MD step), (3) if positions_old in different image than x_unc, dx spans images. Boundary scenario: O/H straddle box face, integration wraps x_unc near L_box, SETTLE reconstructs x_con in old frame, raw dx before minimum-image can be ~±L_box. After minimum-image correction: dx/box in [-1, 1] or wider. Tie-point region (0.5,1) ∪ (-1,-0.5) definitely REACHABLE. Verdict: REACHABLE.

REACHABLE. The jnp.round -> jnp.floor tie-point mechanism is reachable via L1276/L1328 (and secondarily L772/L775). The code correctly uses jnp.round to handle full-box displacements; jnp.floor would fail on these cases. This is not dead code—it is load-bearing for liquid-density MD stability.
